lessons.title: Navigate and calculate
lessons.task: Open RUN-MATRIX and calculate 2 + 3 × 4. Predict the answer before pressing EXE.

lessons.title: Powers and square roots
lessons.task: Find √(3² + 4²). Use the shifted square key for the root.

lessons.title: Calculate a logarithm
lessons.task: Calculate log₁₀(1000) and explain what the result means.

lessons.title: Evaluate geometric growth
lessons.task: A quantity starts at 100 and grows by 5% per period. Calculate its value after three periods.
lessons.limit: This exercise evaluates the sequence formula in RUN-MATRIX; it does not simulate the separate Recursion application.

lessons.title: Graph a function
lessons.task: Store y = x² − 4 in Y1 and draw its graph. Predict the shape and intercepts.
lessons.limit: The simulator currently uses the fixed window −10 ≤ x ≤ 10 and −10 ≤ y ≤ 10.

lessons.title: Find roots on a graph
lessons.task: Solve x² − 4 = 0 by graphing and finding its x-intercepts.
lessons.limit: Only roots within the simulator’s fixed search window [−10, 10] are sought.

lessons.title: Find intersections
lessons.task: Find where y = x² − 4 meets y = 2x + 1.

lessons.title: Locate a minimum
lessons.task: Find the minimum of y = x² − 4 and connect it with the turning point.
lessons.limit: The extremum is found within the fixed model window, not over every real x.

lessons.title: Use a graph for optimisation
lessons.task: A rectangle has area A(x) = x(4 − x), with 0 ≤ x ≤ 4. Locate its maximum and check the endpoint areas.
lessons.limit: This example’s feasible domain and turning point fit the fixed graph window. Always check the problem’s constraints and endpoints.

lessons.title: Pythagoras with the root key
lessons.task: A right triangle has legs 3 and 4. Calculate the hypotenuse, keeping both squares inside the root.

lessons.title: Trigonometry in degrees
lessons.task: A 12 m ladder makes a 35° angle with the ground. Calculate the vertical height 12 sin(35°).

lessons.title: Find an angle using inverse tangent
lessons.task: In a right triangle, opposite/adjacent = 3/4. Find the angle in degrees.

lessons.title: One-variable statistics
lessons.task: Enter 4, 7, 8, 8, 10 and 13 in List 1. Find the mean and compare population and sample standard deviations.

lessons.title: Linear regression and correlation
lessons.task: Fit y = ax + b to (1,3), (2,5), (3,7). Read the coefficients and correlation.

lessons.title: Normal probability between bounds
lessons.task: For Z ~ N(0,1), calculate P(−1.96 ≤ Z ≤ 1.96). Predict whether the area is close to 95%.

lessons.title: An exact binomial probability
lessons.task: If X ~ B(10, 0.5), calculate P(X = 3).

lessons.title: A cumulative binomial probability
lessons.task: If X ~ B(10, 0.5), calculate P(0 ≤ X ≤ 3).

lessons.title: Compound interest with TVM
lessons.task: Invest 100 for two years at 4% nominal annual interest compounded quarterly. Use n = 8 and P/Y = C/Y = 4 to find FV.

lessons.title: Approximate an instantaneous rate
lessons.task: Estimate f′(3) for f(x) = x² using [f(3.001) − f(3)] / 0.001.
lessons.limit: This is a finite-difference exercise in RUN-MATRIX. The native d/dx calculator procedure remains a separate manual outline.

lessons.title: Estimate an area numerically
lessons.task: Estimate ∫₀² x² dx with trapezoids of width 1. The sampled values are 0, 1 and 4.
lessons.limit: This is a trapezoidal-rule exercise, not the simulator’s native definite-integral command. That device-specific manual procedure is still pending.
